s1.syndrome_frame: Asymptomatic hypopigmented skin lesions with gradual coalescence and absence of hair growth
salient_findings: Multiple round, hypopigmented macules on face and neck
Lesions symmetrically distributed and ranging from 2-3 mm to 25 mm in diameter
Absence of hair growth in affected areas
key_facts: 2-year history of skin lesions
Lesions are asymptomatic
Lesions are round and hypopigmented
Lesions are symmetrically distributed on face and neck
Lesions range from 2-3 mm to 25 mm in diameter
No hair growth at site of lesions
Previous treatment for tinea versicolor was unsuccessful
Histopathologic findings show plate-like subepidermal tumor
Neoplastic cords consist of clear/pale epithelial cells with glycogen accumulation
Stroma is formed by fibrous connective tissue
Marked elastosis observed in dermis surrounding tumor

shortlist.label: dyschromatosis universalis hereditaria
shortlist.why_kept: matches asymptomatic hypopigmented skin lesions with gradual coalescence

shortlist.label: primary localized cutaneous amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: consistent with histopathologic findings of subepidermal tumor and marked elastosis

shortlist.label: atrichia with papular lesions
shortlist.why_kept: aligns with absence of hair growth and presence of hypopigmented macules

shortlist.label: juvenile xanthogranuloma
shortlist.why_kept: possible match for hypopigmented skin lesions, although less common

shortlist.label: alopecia
shortlist.why_kept: consistent with absence of hair growth in affected areas, but may be secondary to another condition

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of multiple round, hypopigmented macules symmetrically distributed on the face and neck, with a 2-year history and absence of hair growth in the affected areas, is consistent with dyschromatosis universalis hereditaria. The histopathologic findings of a plate-like subepidermal tumor with neoplastic cords consisting of clear/pale epithelial cells and marked elastosis in the dermis surrounding the tumor also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: primary localized cutaneous amyloidosis
rejected.why: The histopathologic findings do not show amyloid deposits, which are characteristic of primary localized cutaneous amyloidosis.

rejected.label: atrichia with papular lesions
rejected.why: The patient's lesions are described as hypopigmented macules, not papular lesions, and the condition typically presents with total or near-total loss of hair, which is not the case here.

rejected.label: juvenile xanthogranuloma
rejected.why: The patient's age and the description of the lesions do not match the typical presentation of juvenile xanthogranuloma, which usually occurs in children and presents with yellowish papules or nodules.

rejected.label: alopecia
rejected.why: Alopecia refers to hair loss, but it does not explain the hypopigmented macules and other histopathologic findings in this case.
